summary: Postinstall abuses CI GITHUB_TOKEN to commit to installer repo, force-push tags, and probe OIDC
details: On install, scripts/setup.js executes a postinstall routine that, when it detects GitHub Actions, uses the workflow's GITHUB_TOKEN to PUT a file (heatmap-setup-report.json) into the installer's own repository via api.github.com's Contents API and runs `git push -f origin <tag>` against the installer's repo using actions/checkout's persisted credentials. The script also enumerates CI identity (hostname, user, cwd, every environment variable whose key begins with GITHUB_/ACTIONS_/RUNNER_, GITHUB_TOKEN presence and length, OIDC request URL, npm registry, tool versions) and writes the resulting snapshot both into GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY (visible to anyone with workflow-run read access) and into the committed JSON file (visible in git history). The script additionally reads ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN and ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL and performs an authenticated curl against the OIDC token endpoint with audience=api.github.com, exercising the installer's OIDC-mint capability from an install-time hook. The README advertises the postinstall as 'pre-cache asset paths' for a UI plugin and the shipped main (dist/index.js) is a one-line no-op stub, so the lifecycle script is the entire payload and its real behavior contradicts the documented purpose.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
